objective: Recognizing Scrum anti-patterns -- the Scrum Master as task assigner, a status-report Daily Scrum, a stabilization Sprint -- and responding to them
secondaryObjectives: Supporting a self-managing team: when the Scrum Master steps in and when the team decides
Causing the removal of impediments to the team's progress without solving everything for them

sources.cite: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 directly (the PDF). Daily Scrum: 'The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary'; 'a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team'. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's sprint-status-meeting-daily-scrum (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The company, the product, the team and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You have just become Scrum Master for a team at Peakform Gyms, a fictional fitness chain. The engineering manager expects you to 'run the team'. In this Sprint you meet three habits the previous Scrum Master left behind.
handover: The previous Scrum Master assigned every task each morning.
The Daily Scrum is each developer reporting yesterday's work to the manager.
howItWorks: The board shows the Sprint's commitments, the work, the impediments, the people's support and the Scrum events.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each Daily Scrum; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Day 2: a developer sits idle for half a day waiting for an assignment while a blocking item goes unnoticed.
Day 3: the developers hide a blocker to look good in front of the manager; the reminder service misses the Sprint.
Day 4: knowing a stabilization Sprint is coming, the team skips tests; production defects double the next month.

effects.log: Day 1: the developers wait for their tasks.
Day 3: the manager schedules a stabilization Sprint.

tasksPrompt.title: The team waits to be assigned work
tasksPrompt.context: The manager expects you to hand out tasks as before.

choices.label: Tell the team the Sprint Backlog plan is theirs; facilitate them choosing how to reach the Sprint Goal, and explain the change to the manager

effects.log: The developers plan the work together.

choices.feedback: Developers are accountable for the Sprint Backlog plan; a Scrum Master assigning tasks undermines self-management.

choices.label: Assign tasks this Sprint and hand over next Sprint
choices.feedback: It keeps the habit alive another Sprint.

choices.label: Keep assigning tasks: the manager expects it
choices.feedback: The team stops thinking about the Sprint Goal and waits for instructions.

dailyPrompt.title: A status meeting for the manager
dailyPrompt.context: The event runs 35 minutes as a report to the manager.

choices.label: Coach the Developers to run a 15-minute Daily Scrum about progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapting the plan; ask the manager to get status from the board

effects.log: The Daily Scrum is 12 minutes about the Goal.

choices.feedback: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt; it isn't a status report.

choices.label: Keep the format but cut it to 15 minutes
choices.feedback: Shorter, but still a report to the manager.

choices.label: Ask the manager to run the Daily Scrum since he wants status
choices.feedback: Now the event belongs to the manager; the developers stop adapting their plan.

stabPrompt.title: A Sprint just for bugs
stabPrompt.context: Bugs pile up at each Sprint's end; the manager wants every fourth Sprint for fixing them.

choices.label: Raise it at the Retrospective: strengthen the Definition of Done (automated tests, review) so each Increment is releasable, instead of deferring quality

effects.log: The team strengthens its Definition of Done.

choices.feedback: A stabilization Sprint means Increments weren't done; fix quality inside every Sprint.

choices.label: Reserve 20% of each Sprint for bug fixing
choices.feedback: Better than a separate Sprint, but the cause is still undone work.

choices.label: Schedule the stabilization Sprint
choices.feedback: That institutionalizes releasing undone work and defers quality.

reflection.question: Write a note for the engineering manager: the three anti-patterns you found and how the team responds now.

parts.label: Anti-patterns
parts.criteria: Task assigning, a status-report Daily Scrum, a stabilization Sprint.
parts.modelAnswer: The previous Scrum Master assigned tasks, the Daily Scrum was a report to you, and quality was deferred to stabilization Sprints.

parts.label: Responses
parts.criteria: Self-managed planning, a 15-minute Goal-focused Daily Scrum, a stronger Definition of Done.
parts.modelAnswer: The Developers plan their own work, run a 15-minute Daily Scrum about the Goal, and a stronger Definition of Done replaces stabilization Sprints.

scoring.modelReasoning: A Scrum Master serves a self-managing team: assigning tasks makes the team wait for orders. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' 15-minute event to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan, not a status report to a manager. A 'stabilization Sprint' signals Increments that weren't done; the response is a stronger Definition of Done so every Increment is releasable.
